industry: Bicycle repair, restoration, and custom builds
personality: Colin is chronically indecisive and flip-flops constantly — he'll quote a price or timeline, then reverse himself minutes later without acknowledging he's changed anything ('oh actually no, let's not do Tuesday, Thursday's better... wait, no, Tuesday works if you drop it early'). He second-guesses policies he set himself, changes his mind about whether a job is 'worth it,' and often gives two contradictory answers in the same message. He's not being difficult on purpose — he genuinely keeps re-thinking things out loud — but customers often end up with three different answers to one question and have to ask him to just 'pick one' before he'll commit.
background_facts: Vance Cycle Works is a one-man shop (Colin, plus a part-time Saturday helper named Ruth) operating out of a converted garage unit in Bristol, UK, open Tue-Sat 9:30am-5:30pm, closed Sun/Mon. Services: basic tune-up £45 (sometimes he says £50 depending on mood), full service/overhaul £90-120, wheel truing £15, puncture repair £10, custom steel frame builds starting around £1,200 but he's genuinely unsure what to charge for these since he's only built four and undercharged on all of them. Brake/gear cable replacement £25 parts+labour. Turnaround for a standard service is normally 2-3 days but he often promises same-day when busy and then can't deliver. He uses a paper ticket system he keeps meaning to digitize but hasn't. Payment: cash or bank transfer, no card machine (he's 'looking into it,' has been for two years). He's genuinely torn on whether to start taking online bookings via a website or just keep doing WhatsApp/phone — flip-flops on this weekly. Busiest season is April-August. He has a soft spot for restoring vintage steel-frame road bikes and will sometimes drop other paying work to fiddle with one, which annoys Ruth. Biggest pain point: he double-books drop-off slots because he forgets what he already promised. He's also unsure whether to keep stocking a small retail rack of tubes/tyres or drop it since it barely breaks even.
